headline: 34-run win: Bangladesh reach Asia Cup semifinals after beating UAE
summary: Despite a shaky batting start, a dominant bowling performance secures Bangladesh's spot in the semifinals, where they will face India.
details: Bangladesh secured a place in the Women’s Asia Cup T20 semifinals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 34 runs in their final Group B match in Dubai.
The victory was hard-fought, as Bangladesh struggled early in their batting innings, falling to 55-6 in the 12th over.
Experienced batter Sharmin Akhter Supta saved the day with a crucial 38 off 31 balls, helping Bangladesh post a total of 103-9.
The bowling unit then took control, with Marufa Akter striking twice early to dismantle the UAE top order.
Spinners Rabeya Khan (3-14) and Nahida Akter (2-18) tightened the grip, restricting the hosts to just 69-9 from their 20 overs.
Bangladesh now advances as Group B runners-up and is set to clash with India in the first semifinal this Thursday at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.
caption:
From 55-6 to the semifinals! 🇧🇩
Bangladesh survives a UAE scare to keep their Asia Cup dreams alive.

Bangladesh secured a place in the Women’s Asia Cup T20 semifinals after defeating the United Arab Emirates by 34 runs in their final Group B match in Dubai.

The victory was hard-fought, as Bangladesh struggled early in their batting innings, falling to 55-6 in the 12th over.

Experienced batter Sharmin Akhter Supta saved the day with a crucial 38 off 31 balls, helping Bangladesh post a total of 103-9.

The bowling unit then took control, with Marufa Akter striking twice early to dismantle the UAE top order.

Spinners Rabeya Khan (3-14) and Nahida Akter (2-18) tightened the grip, restricting the hosts to just 69-9 from their 20 overs.

Bangladesh now advances as Group B runners-up and is set to clash with India in the first semifinal this Thursday at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.

headline_marked: Parliament adopts motion to [[bring former IGP Benazir Ahmed back]] from UAE
headline: Parliament adopts motion to bring former IGP Benazir Ahmed back from UAE
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed assures the House that the government will show 'no leniency' in extraditing the 'serial killer' former police chief.
details: Parliament has adopted an opposition-backed motion requiring Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to brief the House on the extradition process of former IGP Benazir Ahmed from the UAE.
During the debate, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed described Benazir Ahmed as a 'serial killer' and stated that the government would show 'no leniency' in bringing him back to face justice.
The Home Minister revealed that an Interpol Red Notice is active against Benazir, and the National Central Bureau in Abu Dhabi confirmed his arrest in the UAE on June 12, 2026.
Opposition members, including Jamaat MP Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem, questioned the government's sincerity, citing reports that Benazir had secured bail and fled to Saint Lucia.
However, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that UAE officials confirmed Benazir remains in the UAE and has not departed for a third country.
The government is currently working to verify allegations of passport fraud and identify illegal assets held by the former IGP both at home and abroad.
Opposition leaders also proposed the formation of a special cell dedicated to handling the cases of Benazir and other fugitive 'fascists' who have fled the country.
caption:
Home Minister calls former IGP Benazir Ahmed a 'serial killer' as Parliament demands an update on his extradition from the UAE.

Parliament has adopted an opposition-backed motion requiring Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to brief the House on the extradition process of former IGP Benazir Ahmed from the UAE.

During the debate, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed described Benazir Ahmed as a 'serial killer' and stated that the government would show 'no leniency' in bringing him back to face justice.

The Home Minister revealed that an Interpol Red Notice is active against Benazir, and the National Central Bureau in Abu Dhabi confirmed his arrest in the UAE on June 12, 2026.

Opposition members, including Jamaat MP Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem, questioned the government's sincerity, citing reports that Benazir had secured bail and fled to Saint Lucia.

However, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir clarified that UAE officials confirmed Benazir remains in the UAE and has not departed for a third country.

The government is currently working to verify allegations of passport fraud and identify illegal assets held by the former IGP both at home and abroad.

Opposition leaders also proposed the formation of a special cell dedicated to handling the cases of Benazir and other fugitive 'fascists' who have fled the country.
